title: Kernel of restriction generated by boundary inertia
statement: Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected separated curve of finite type over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion, and put $S_0=C_0\setminus U_0$. Let $W(U_0)\to W(C_0)$ be the degree-preserving homomorphism of Weil groups induced by $j_0$, and for each $x\in S_0$ let $I_x$ be the local inertia subgroup in the decomposition-group map of [d-real-boundary]. Then the kernel of $W(U_0)\to W(C_0)$ is the smallest closed normal subgroup of $W(U_0)$ containing the images of all $I_x$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia, specialized from the function-field fundamental group to a dense open of the normal integral curve; the passage to Weil groups uses the degree-compatible surjection of lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective.

proof.text: The curves $C_0$ and $U_0$ are normal by lem-sc-smooth-normal. They are Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian (the base is the spectrum of a field). A connected nonempty normal Noetherian scheme is integral: the disjoint open integral components in rem-pc-regular-normal (2) leave only one component. Apply this to $C_0$; its nonempty open $U_0$ is then integral and has the same generic point and function field $K$. Fix a separable closure $\Omega/K$, choose an algebraic closure $\widetilde\Omega$ containing $\Omega$ and use $\operatorname{Spec}\widetilde\Omega$ as geometric generic base point (automorphisms extend uniquely over the purely inseparable extension), and write $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$, $P=\pi_1(U_0)$ and $Q=\pi_1(C_0)$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, hypothesis normal integral; preparation from the cited curve and Noetherian lemmas.

proof.text: Apply lem-dl-a1-normal-scheme-galois-inertia-presentation to $U_0$ and $C_0$ using the same $\Omega$. Obtain continuous surjections $a:G\to P$, $b:G\to Q$ with kernels $N_U,N_C$. Functoriality gives $b=f\circ a$ for restriction $f:P\to Q$: on every finite etale cover both sides act on its generic geometric fibre by the same field automorphism. Choose identical local strict henselizations and embeddings at points of $U_0$, whose local rings in the two schemes agree. The cited presentation says that $N_U$ and $N_C$ are respectively the closed normal closures of $J_x=\operatorname{Aut}_{K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega)$ for $x\in U_0$ and $x\in C_0$.

For each boundary point $x$, apply lem-dl-a1-henselian-global-inertia-comparison with the normal local ring $A=\mathcal O_{C_0,x}$. Its comparison identifies $J_x$ with the inertia kernel in $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline K_x/K_x)$ of d-real-boundary, where $K_x=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\mathrm h})$. The map of this local group into $P$ is the composite through $G$: on a finite cover of $U_0$ its fibre is evaluated by precisely the same field automorphism of $\Omega$, by lem-galois-pi1-functoriality. Thus $a(J_x)$ is the prescribed inertia image for a compatible path. An arbitrary path in d-real-boundary conjugates that image in $P$; closed normal generation in $P$ is unchanged by replacing each generator subgroup by a conjugate. Write $L_x$ for the prescribed image in $P$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, identification of the top row and the residue kernel; Tag 0BTD, clause (3).

proof.text: Let $N=\ker f$. Surjectivity of $a$ and $b=fa$ give $N=a(N_C)$: lift $p\in N$ to $g\in G$, then $b(g)=f(p)=1$. Since $N_C$ is compact, its image is closed; it is normal because $a$ is surjective. Its generators from $U_0$ vanish under $a$, so $N$ is the closed normal closure in $P$ of the $L_x$ for $x\in S_0$. Explicitly, if $T\subseteq P$ is closed normal and contains every $L_x$, then $a^{-1}(T)$ contains every $J_x$ for $x\in C_0$ (the ones in $U_0$ lie in $N_U$). The presentation forces $N_C\subseteq a^{-1}(T)$, hence $N\subseteq T$. Conversely each $L_x$ lies in $N$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, quotient by the generators supported on the removed points.

proof.text: The map of Weil groups is the restriction of $f$, with the same degree coordinate, by lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective (2). The pullback description in def-wf-fundamental-representation shows that its kernel is exactly $N$: if $f(p)=1$, its arithmetic degree is zero, so $(p,0)$ belongs to $W(U_0)$ and maps to the identity. Conversely a Weil element in the kernel has degree zero and arithmetic component in $N$. Each $L_x$ lies in the geometric subgroup by lem-real-boundary-decomposition-landing. Let $H$ be its closed normal closure in $W(U_0)$. The kernel just identified is closed normal, hence $H\subseteq N$. The degree-zero subgroup has its compact profinite topology, so $H$, closed therein, is compact and its image is closed in the Hausdorff group $P$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, passage to the Weil pullback; the cited Weil definitions specify the topology.

proof.text: Fix $x\in S_0$ and let $D_x\subseteq P$ be the image of its local absolute Galois group for the prescribed path. Write $r:P\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ for the arithmetic projection. By lem-real-boundary-local-constants, $\kappa(x)/k_0$ is finite and $r(D_x)=\operatorname{Gal}(k/\kappa(x))$. For any $g\in P$, lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius gives an integer $n$ such that $r(g)|_{\kappa(x)}=\Phi^n|_{\kappa(x)}$, where $\Phi$ is geometric Frobenius (the inverse of the cyclic generator in that lemma). Thus $r(g)\Phi^{-n}$ fixes $\kappa(x)$; choose $d\in D_x$ with $r(d)=r(g)\Phi^{-n}$. Then $w=gd^{-1}$ has arithmetic projection $\Phi^n$ and belongs to $W(U_0)$. Since local inertia is a kernel, $D_x$ normalizes $L_x$, so $gL_xg^{-1}=wL_xw^{-1}\subseteq H$. The closed subgroup $H$ of $P$ therefore contains every $P$-conjugate of every $L_x$, hence contains their closed generated subgroup $N$ from step 4. With $H\subseteq N$ this proves equality. If $S_0$ is empty, step 4 gives $N=1$ directly and both normal closures are trivial.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, local inertia normal in decomposition; the finite-field arithmetic projection is given by lem-real-boundary-local-constants.
